name: Demand Charge Exposure Unknown
applicable_contexts: cost story may not track annual consumption
trigger_conditions: annual consumption may be an incomplete cost proxy
anti_triggers: tariff confirms demand charges are immaterial
physical_basis: A site's cost structure can be shaped by when load occurs rather than only by how much annual energy is consumed.
operational_basis: Charging, staging, HVAC, refrigeration, process starts or dispatch duty can create concentrated peaks that do not show up in simple intensity metrics.
financial_mechanism: Demand charges can make timing and orchestration more important than annual kWh.
typical_false_assumption: High energy cost means high energy waste.
hypothesis: Demand-charge exposure may be materially affecting cost, so consumption-first framing may be misreading the dominant variable.
rival_hypotheses: annual consumption is the real dominant cost driver
tariff has little or no demand sensitivity
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: bills or tariff show meaningful demand sensitivity
peak-forming load timing overlaps cost exposure
falsification_conditions: flat profile or low peak concentration
load mix does not support the framing
allowed_claim_language: Demand-charge exposure is a plausible financial translation that should be bounded before efficiency-first underwriting.
financial_exposure_if_false: attention should shift to rival cost drivers
stop_conditions: utility bills and tariff are bounded enough to rank demand sensitivity
escalation_conditions: interval data requested only if bills and tariff still leave material ambiguity
claim_permissions_impact: block ROI framing before tariff validation
example_outputs: The cost driver may be peak timing, not annual consumption.
tests: warehouse and manufacturing acceptance bundles should admit this when tariff and bills remain unresolved
pattern must stay bounded as a financial translation, not a local diagnosis
